title: The city of the dancing lights report on the annual festival of the arts
summary: This collection gathers a set of satirical and speculative pieces, several built around an imagined Annual Festival of the Arts in which art has become spectacle, commerce and provocation. The opening piece is a journalist's report on the festival: a virtual-reality artist turned emotion sculptor, a book designed to decompose into dust after an expiry date, a human race of indebted runners bound across generations, and a closing zeppelin spectacle over San Francisco that is staged as an earthquake and urban collapse. Other stories follow more personal, unsettling situations. A lonely old man refuses to leave a flooded, abandoned city and meets a documentary film crew who see him as a prop for their artistic ambitions. A family of technology-saturated households confronts a son who has made a crude wooden horse by hand. A narrator pursues an obsession with a woman on a vanished island resort whose travel records have disappeared. The pieces share a wry, uneasy tone about art, consumerism, ecological collapse and the loss of human connection. The excerpts suggest a writer who uses a clipped, detailed prose style and dark humour to examine how people and cultures treat experience as something to be packaged and consumed.
